structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the surface of a resting biconcave mammalian red blood cell has mean curvature that varies measurably from point to point, so it is not a constant-mean-curvature surface. The cell also becomes spherical in hypotonic medium, which implicates osmotic or membrane-elastic forces rather than surface tension alone.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In calibrated 3D reconstructions (voxel size 100 nm or finer) of at least 100 normal discocytes in isotonic medium, the coefficient of variation of local mean curvature over the membrane surface exceeds 0.5 for at least 95% of cells, and mean curvature changes sign between the dimple and the rim. In the same preparation diluted to 150 mOsm/kg or below, at least 90% of cells have sphericity above 0.9.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if at least 20% of isotonic discocytes have a mean-curvature coefficient of variation of 0.15 or less, with no sign change, once measurement noise is accounted for. It is also refuted if cells stay biconcave (sphericity below 0.8) in hypotonic dilution.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'surface of equilibrium' under surface tension alone is a surface of constant mean curvature, as in a Plateau or Delaunay figure. His 'fluid drop' means a liquid body whose shape is set only by interfacial tension. His 'diluted blood' means a hypotonic medium, and his 'osmotic inequilibrium' maps onto osmotic pressure and volume regulation. His 'fluid-crystal forces of cholesterin-like constituents' maps onto modern membrane bending elasticity, in the Helfrich and spectrin-cytoskeleton picture. The measurable quantity is the distribution of local mean curvature H over a segmented 3D RBC surface, plus sphericity versus tonicity. One caveat on the test: constant H would be expected for a pure tension-only drop with a pressure difference. The reinterpretation is that the membrane has bending rigidity, so non-constant H does not refute a tension component. It only shows tension alone does not set the shape.

Candidates such as the Cell Image Library, the Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection and MorphoSource were not checked for matching RBC 3D data.
